[2026-06-17] WSN Group
### Kay’s Pest Management Opportunity
- Target: small NYC rodent-focused pest co., ~$1.5M revenue, ~$500K EBITDA, ~30% margins
    - Owner has run it 20 years, lifestyle operator, not growth-minded, shows up as a technician
    - Recent client win: Cartier, strong alignment on high-discretion, luxury service
    - Prior offer: ~$2.5M (declined due to capital gains, broker fees, pre-college kids)
- Thesis: high-end, high-discretion pest control for luxury retail, hospitality, corporate in NYC
    - Wedge: rodent specialist, not generalist, NYC density is a natural tailwind
    - Cartier as proof point, expand to other luxury houses
- Key tension: very small platform, no infrastructure to scale from
    - High margins but low cost base means no operating leverage to grow from
    - Bigger platform ($7M revenue, same EBITDA) would have had more built-in leverage
### Approaching the Coffee Meeting
- Go in with a model and a structure in mind, but lead with listening
    - Ask what he wants to optimize for: financial, professional, emotional
    - Owners rarely get asked about their business; he’ll likely open up unprompted
- Owner profile: product/technical person, not a sales or growth operator
    - Cares about clients above all, college costs on a 5-year horizon
    - More likely motivated by long-term wealth creation than upfront cash
- Frame rollover equity as the pitch: he keeps upside as the business scales
    - Don’t lead with 20%; let him argue up from a lower anchor
    - Consulting/transition fee also on the table as a sweetener
- On the name (currently “TEX”): don’t over-index on it
    - Suss out what he sees as his legacy (discretion, service, reliability) and affirm that’s the brand being preserved
### LOI and Offer Sequencing
- Submit the LOI before the in-person meeting, then schedule the meeting same day or next
    - Lets you walk through it together, catch misreads, adjust phrasing in real time
    - Avoids the cold-read emotional reaction (“all my years of work are worth X”)
- After coffee: if he’s aligned on structure, submit the offer quickly
    - Test key questions openly: rollover equity, seller note, transition timeline
### Roll-up Model and Capital Strategy
- Single acquisition too small to stand alone; likely needs multi-acquisition or de novo build
    - Acquihire approach: buy technicians + client lists at lower multiples, no heavy capex
    - Organic growth possible (new accounts, expanded services) but not sufficient alone
- Raise committed capital alongside or concurrent with closing the first deal
    - Committed capital model could support a normalized salary rather than a compressed one
    - Carry on the fund side offsets the squeeze from a small first platform
- Hire an M&A-focused resource early (potential chief of staff with PE background already identified)
    - Operating the first business while sourcing tuck-ins simultaneously is the core execution risk
### Investor Considerations
- Expect pushback on deal size from most investors; some (e.g. Trilogy, min. ~$1M check) may sit out
    - A few committed believers can cover the equity check even if others pass
    - Detroit-based investor (smallest on cap table) most engaged: knows the market and manufacturing
- Lacey Wismer (Lacey Hunter): family office, longer horizon, focus on female entrepreneurs, very direct
    - Sarah Rosenthal (already on cap table) is close friends with Lacey, good warm path
    - Worth a conversation even without asking for money, she’ll tell you exactly what she thinks
- Kent Weaver: enthusiastic in the moment but hard to pin down post-close; useful for capital, less so for ongoing support
### Megan: Under LOI, Diligence Update
- Signed LOI last Monday, flew to Detroit Wednesday to rebuild seller relationship in person
    - Two-month gap during lawyer/broker phase had cooled direct contact
    - Left both days more excited about the business than when she arrived
- Diligence approach: five key commercial bets to resolve by end of June before spending on QofE
    - Weekly investor emails; individual meetings to surface key risks and questions early
    - Documents requested day one, still waiting; broker expects delivery today
- Investor landscape: 10 total
    - Two clearly in (incl. Detroit family office), one likely out, others warm but uncommitted
    - Trilogy and Next Coast most active in diligence; Next Coast split (Tatiana in, Anthony skeptical on construction cyclicality)
- On sharing data room with non-cap-table investors: consensus is don’t, but informal “keeping you posted” outreach is fine
    - If confirmed outs emerge, get verbal okay from leaning-in investors before approaching new names
### Next Steps
- Build a roll-up model (multi-acquisition structure, committed capital raise, salary assumptions)
- Prep for coffee meeting: model an offer range, draft rollover equity framing, seller note options
- Reach out to Lacey Wismer for a conversation (via Sarah Rosenthal warm intro)
- Attempt to re-engage Kent Weaver
Key takeaways:
- Premium service wedge is the clearest differentiator.
- Verify true cash flow and owner draw before advancing.
- Cartier is a useful proof point for the luxury-service pitch.
